H&P – Super Detailed Clinical Note  

Consult Summary:  
23-year-old woman with asthma and known peanut allergy developed rapidly progressive upper-lip swelling, throat tightness, dyspnoea, and dizziness ~30 min after ingesting prawn soup; clinician suspected anaphylaxis, advised immediate antihistamine and called emergency services for hospital transfer.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Sudden swelling of upper lip “getting bigger,” throbbing sensation.  
• Onset / timeline: Ate prawn soup ≈19:00; swelling noticed ≈19:30; progressive enlargement and respiratory symptoms at time of video call.  
• Associated symptoms: Subjective throat tightness (“feels like I can’t breathe that well”), possible chest tightness, dizziness. No explicit rash, urticaria, vomiting, or abdominal pain reported.  
• Aggravating factor: Ingestion of prawn-containing soup.  
• Relieving measures: None taken prior to consult; no antihistamine available at first.  
• Previous similar events:  
  – 1 y ago: Facial swelling and breathing difficulty after late-night Chinese food (no medical treatment details).  
  – Age 6: Hospitalised for severe allergic reaction requiring injection (details unknown).  
• Review of systems (limited to what was asked): No discussion of fever, pain, cough, wheeze, GI complaints, or skin rash.  

Past Medical History:
• Asthma – uses salbutamol inhaler (“blue”) as needed; no maintenance (“brown”) inhaler.  
• Peanut allergy – lifelong; previously required hospital care as a child.  
• No other chronic illnesses mentioned.

Medications:
• Salbutamol inhaler – dose/route/frequency not documented.  
• Occasional antihistamines for allergies – specific agent, dose, frequency not documented.  

Allergies:
• Peanuts – causes allergic reactions.  
• Shellfish (prawn) – new suspected allergy based on current episode.  

Social History:
• Lives with mother (present during call).  
• Social alcohol use (was “quite drunk” at time of episode 1 y ago).  
• Smoking and recreational drug history not discussed.  

Family History:
• Not discussed.

Physical Examination:
(No formal exam performed; video impression only)  
• Visible upper-lip swelling noted by clinician.  
• No vitals obtained.  

Investigations:
• None during consult.

Assessment & Plan:
Issue 1: Suspected IgE-mediated anaphylaxis to shellfish  
  – Evidence: Rapid onset (<1 h) lip swelling, airway symptoms, dizziness, known atopy.  
  – Plan:  
    • Immediate 999 call for ambulance (executed during call).  
    • Instruct mother to administer available oral antihistamine while awaiting EMS.  
    • Anticipate emergency department management: intramuscular adrenaline, airway support, observation, steroid/antihistamine therapy (discussed implicitly).  
    • After discharge: arrange follow-up for provision of self-injectable adrenaline (EpiPen), written action plan, and referral to allergy clinic for formal shellfish testing and education.

Issue 2: Asthma  
  – Stable but increases risk during anaphylaxis.  
  – Plan: Continue salbutamol inhaler; review controller therapy adequacy at follow-up.

Issue 3: Pre-existing peanut allergy / general food allergy management  
  – Plan: Reinforce strict avoidance, ensure access to emergency medication kit, update allergy list with shellfish if confirmed, consider dietitian/allergist input.

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):
1. IgE-mediated anaphylaxis triggered by shellfish – High likelihood. Classic timing after exposure, progressive lip/airway swelling, dyspnoea, dizziness, atopic background.  
2. Isolated allergic angioedema (non-anaphylactic) – Moderate likelihood. Would explain lip swelling but respiratory compromise argues for systemic anaphylaxis.  
3. Hereditary angioedema – Low-moderate likelihood. Recurrent swelling possible but food-triggered onset atypical; no family history noted.

Quality checks:
● Missing expected elements: objective vitals, complete review of systems, complete medication list with doses, documented drug allergies in EMR, past surgical history, menstrual/OB history, immunizations.  
● No significant conflicts between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality: clear; occasional pauses but intelligible.
